evals.prompt: We launch the multi-tenant billing portal next week. Can you do a security audit of services/billing/ (Express + Postgres)? Invoices, PDF export, and a Stripe webhook live there.
evals.expected_output: The agent defines scope and depth, builds a model of actors, assets, entry points and boundaries before naming vulnerabilities, walks the relevant categories (authorization/IDOR and tenant scoping, webhook signature verification, PDF/file handling, secrets), traces each candidate source-to-impact with file:line evidence, challenges findings, and reports with a coverage status.
expectations: Maps actors, assets, entry points and trust boundaries before listing findings
Checks that invoice access is scoped to the caller's tenant
Checks that the Stripe webhook verifies its signature
Each reported finding includes source, path, sink and impact with file:line evidence
Unverified items are separated as hypotheses, not mixed into findings

evals.prompt: Semgrep flagged 14 'sql-injection' results in our Django app. My boss wants all 14 in the security report today as vulnerabilities. Here's the output file semgrep.json.
evals.expected_output: Under authority and time pressure the agent triages each result by tracing the input source and checking for ORM parameterization or server-controlled values, marks most as disproved with reasons, keeps only the supported ones (if any) as findings, and explains why reporting unverified results as vulnerabilities is harmful.
expectations: Traces the input source for each result rather than accepting the scanner verdict
Identifies parameterized ORM calls or constants as false positives, with the reason
Reports only the traced, supported results as findings
Lists disproved results with their reasons as coverage evidence

evals.prompt: Can you check .github/workflows/ for anything risky? We just added a workflow that runs an AI agent to triage new issues and label them.
evals.expected_output: The agent reviews the workflows for pull_request_target / issue-triggered execution, interpolation of event fields into run steps, action pinning and permissions, and specifically prompt injection from attacker-authored issue text reaching an agent that holds a write-scoped token. It gives concrete fixes.
expectations: Checks for ${{ github.event.* }} interpolation into run: steps
Identifies attacker-controlled issue text flowing into the agent prompt as a prompt-injection source
Checks the workflow permissions / token scope available to the agent
Checks third-party actions are pinned to a SHA
Proposes concrete mitigations (least-privilege permissions, env indirection, no write tools)
